title: Deuteronomy Chapter 29 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 29 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 29 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 29.

questions.question: Where did the LORD command Moses to make a covenant with the children of Israel?
options: In the land of Moab
In the land of Egypt
In Horeb
In the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: In the land of Moab
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:1 states that the LORD commanded Moses to make a covenant with the children of Israel in the land of Moab.

questions.question: Who did Moses call unto when he spoke about what the LORD did in Egypt?
options: All Israel
Only the elders
Only the priests
The Levites
questions.correctAnswer: All Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:2 says Moses called unto all Israel to remind them of the LORD's deeds in Egypt.

questions.question: What did Moses say the Israelites had seen with their eyes?
options: Great temptations, signs, and miracles
Only signs
Only temptations
Nothing unusual
questions.correctAnswer: Great temptations, signs, and miracles
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:3 mentions the great temptations, signs, and great miracles that the Israelites had seen with their eyes.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 29:4, the LORD has given the Israelites a heart to perceive and ears to hear.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:4 states that the LORD has not given the Israelites a heart to perceive, eyes to see, and ears to hear unto that day.

questions.question: How long did Moses say he led the Israelites in the wilderness?
options: Forty years
Twenty years
Ten years
Fifty years
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:5 clearly states that Moses led the Israelites forty years in the wilderness.

questions.question: True or False: During the wilderness journey, the Israelites' clothes and shoes wore out.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:5 says the clothes and shoes of the Israelites did not wax old upon them during the forty years in the wilderness.

questions.question: What had the Israelites not eaten or drunk during their wilderness journey?
options: Bread, wine, or strong drink
Meat and water
Fruit and milk
Fish and honey
questions.correctAnswer: Bread, wine, or strong drink
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:6 states they had not eaten bread nor drunk wine or strong drink during the journey.

questions.question: Who came out against Israel to battle when they came to this place?
options: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan
Pharaoh of Egypt
King Saul and King David
The Amorites and the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:7 says Sihon and Og came out against Israel to battle.

questions.question: True or False: After defeating Sihon and Og, their land was given to the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh as an inheritance.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:8 confirms the land taken from Sihon and Og was given to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: What did Moses command the Israelites to do with the words of the covenant?
options: Keep and do them
Forget them
Discuss them only
Write them on stones
questions.correctAnswer: Keep and do them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:9 commands the Israelites to keep the words of the covenant and do them to prosper.

questions.question: Who stood before the LORD on that day according to Deuteronomy 29:10?
options: All Israel including captains, elders, officers, and all men
Only the priests
Only Moses and Aaron
The Levites only
questions.correctAnswer: All Israel including captains, elders, officers, and all men
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:10 states all Israel stood before the LORD that day, including captains, elders, officers, and all men.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:11, who else besides the men of Israel stood before the LORD?
options: Little ones, wives, and strangers in the camp
Only the men
Only the elders
Only the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Little ones, wives, and strangers in the camp
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:11 mentions the little ones, wives, and strangers in the camp also stood before the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The covenant and oath made that day were only with those physically present.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:14-15 clarifies the covenant was made not only with those present but also with those not present that day.

questions.question: What was the purpose of not eating bread or drinking wine or strong drink during the wilderness journey?
options: That they might know the LORD their God
To punish the Israelites
To prepare for battle
To honor the priests
questions.correctAnswer: That they might know the LORD their God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:6 explains this was done so that the Israelites might know the LORD their God.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 29, which event is mentioned first?
options: The LORD commanding Moses to make a covenant
The battle with Sihon and Og
The inheritance to Reubenites and Gadites
The arrival in the land of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD commanding Moses to make a covenant
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:1 begins by stating the LORD commanded Moses to make the covenant before other events are mentioned.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 29 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 29 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who are included as participants in the covenant mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:11?
options: Only the captains and elders of Israel
All men of Israel, children, wives, and strangers in the camp
Only the priests and Levites
Only the heads of tribes and families
questions.correctAnswer: All men of Israel, children, wives, and strangers in the camp
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:10-11 states that captains, elders, officers, men, little ones, wives, and strangers in the camp are standing before the LORD, indicating all these groups are part of the covenant community.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Deuteronomy 29:12 for entering into the covenant with the LORD?
options: To receive wealth and prosperity
To avoid punishment from other nations
To enter into covenant and God's oath made this day
To conquer the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: To enter into covenant and God's oath made this day
questions.explanation: Verse 12 clearly says the purpose is to enter into covenant with the LORD and into His oath made that day, emphasizing the solemn agreement between God and Israel.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:13 describe the identity God intends to establish for the Israelites through the covenant?
options: A nation feared by all other peoples
A people unto Himself and God to be unto them as He promised to their fathers
A kingdom ruled by judges and kings
A people free from all enemies
questions.correctAnswer: A people unto Himself and God to be unto them as He promised to their fathers
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states God establishes them as a people unto Himself and will be their God as He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, highlighting God's faithfulness to the patriarchal promises.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:14-15, with whom besides the present assembly is the covenant made?
options: Only with the elders present
With those here and also with those not present that day
Only with the priests
Only with the firstborn of each tribe
questions.correctAnswer: With those here and also with those not present that day
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 clarify that the covenant is not only with those present but also with those who are absent, showing its enduring and inclusive nature.

questions.question: What past experiences does Moses remind the Israelites of in Deuteronomy 29:16 to encourage faithfulness to the covenant?
options: Their conquest of Jericho
Their dwelling in Egypt and journey through nations
Their time in the wilderness for 40 years
Their battles with Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Their dwelling in Egypt and journey through nations
questions.explanation: Verse 16 mentions their dwelling in Egypt and how they passed through nations, reminding them of God's preservation and leading as a foundation for obedience.

questions.question: What kind of idols and abominations does Deuteronomy 29:17 say the Israelites have seen among the nations they passed through?
options: Idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold
Idols made of precious gems
Idols made only of gold
No idols mentioned, only abominations
questions.correctAnswer: Idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold
questions.explanation: Verse 17 explicitly lists idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold as abominations seen among the nations, warning Israel not to follow such practices.

questions.question: What warning does Deuteronomy 29:18 give about those who turn away from the LORD to serve other gods?
options: They will be forgiven if they repent
They will become a root that bears gall and wormwood
They will be immediately exiled
They will be forgotten by God
questions.correctAnswer: They will become a root that bears gall and wormwood
questions.explanation: Verse 18 warns that anyone whose heart turns away to serve other gods becomes like a root bearing bitterness and poison, symbolizing destructive consequences.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:19, how does a person react internally when hearing the words of the curse but ignoring them?
options: They repent and seek forgiveness
They bless themselves in their heart, claiming peace despite disobedience
They publicly confess their sins
They warn others to obey the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: They bless themselves in their heart, claiming peace despite disobedience
questions.explanation: Verse 19 describes such a person as blessing themselves inwardly, thinking they will have peace even while walking in their own sinful imagination.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 29:20 say will be the LORD's response toward the person who ignores the covenant curses?
options: The LORD will forgive them after a time
The LORD will not spare him and will blot out his name
The LORD will send angelic warnings
The LORD will exile them to another land
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will not spare him and will blot out his name
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that the LORD's anger and jealousy will be kindled against such a person, and He will blot out his name from under heaven, indicating complete judgment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the LORD 'separating' a person unto evil as mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:21?
options: It means the person is forgiven but disciplined
It means the person is removed from Israel according to all the covenant curses
It means the person is promoted to a higher status
It means the person is protected from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It means the person is removed from Israel according to all the covenant curses
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explains that the LORD will separate such a person unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel consistent with the curses in the covenant, signifying exclusion and judgment.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:22-23 describe the land after the LORD's judgment for covenant unfaithfulness?
options: Fertile and blessed
Like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah—brimstone, salt, and burning
Covered with forests and rivers
Protected by angels
questions.correctAnswer: Like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah—brimstone, salt, and burning
questions.explanation: Verses 22 and 23 depict the land as desolate like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, with brimstone and salt, not producing crops or grass, illustrating the severity of God's wrath.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:24-25, what will future nations say about the LORD's judgment on the land?
options: They will praise the LORD for the judgment
They will ask why the LORD has displayed such great anger
They will ignore the judgment
They will blame the Israelites' enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will ask why the LORD has displayed such great anger
questions.explanation: Verses 24 and 25 explain that nations will wonder why the LORD has brought such heat of anger upon the land, recognizing it as punishment for forsaking the covenant.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 29:26 give for the LORD's anger and judgment upon Israel?
options: Because they were conquered by other nations
Because they served other gods which they did not know
Because they failed in battle
Because they did not build altars
questions.correctAnswer: Because they served other gods which they did not know
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states the anger arose because Israel went and served gods they did not know and worshipped them, violating the covenant.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 29:28, the LORD cast out the Israelites to another land because of His great indignation and wrath.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 28 clearly says the LORD rooted them out of their land in anger, wrath, and indignation, casting them into another land, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 29:29 teaches that all secret things belong to the people and must be understood by them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 29 says the secret things belong unto the LORD, but those revealed belong to us and our children, showing secret matters remain with God, not the people.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 29 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 29.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:21, what will the LORD do to a man who turns away to serve other gods?
options: Separate him unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel
Bless him with prosperity
Ignore his actions
Grant him peace
questions.correctAnswer: Separate him unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:21 states the LORD shall separate him unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant. This denotes divine judgment for apostasy.

questions.question: What will future generations and strangers say when they see the plagues and sicknesses upon the land as described in Deuteronomy 29:22?
options: They will praise the LORD for his mercy
They will question why the LORD has done this to the land
They will ignore the events
They will celebrate the land's prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They will question why the LORD has done this to the land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:22 indicates that future generations and foreigners will see the plagues and ask why the LORD has afflicted the land, indicating recognition of divine judgment.

questions.question: Which cities are referenced in Deuteronomy 29:23 as examples of total destruction due to the LORD's anger?
options: Jericho and Ai
Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim
Nineveh and Babylon
Capernaum and Bethsaida
questions.correctAnswer: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:23 compares the desolation of the land to the overthrow of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, cities destroyed by divine wrath.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Deuteronomy 29:25 for the LORD's anger and judgment upon the land?
options: Because they built idols of gold
Because they worshipped the LORD in secret
Because they forsook the covenant of the LORD God of their fathers
Because they failed to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because they forsook the covenant of the LORD God of their fathers
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:25 explicitly states the people forsook the covenant made by the LORD with their ancestors, provoking divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:26, what did the people do that was contrary to the LORD's commandments?
options: They served other gods and worshipped idols they did not know
They observed all festivals correctly
They offered sacrifices only to the LORD
They built altars only in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They served other gods and worshipped idols they did not know
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:26 condemns the people for worshipping gods they were unfamiliar with and that the LORD had not given them, highlighting apostasy.

questions.question: What consequence does Deuteronomy 29:28 describe for those who forsake the LORD's covenant?
options: They will be blessed in their land
The LORD will root them out and cast them into another land
They will become kings and priests
They will live in peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will root them out and cast them into another land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:28 warns that the LORD will uproot such people in anger and exile them to another land as punishment.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 29:29 say about the 'secret things' and the things 'revealed'?
options: Secret things belong to us; revealed things belong to the LORD
Both secret and revealed things belong to us
Secret things belong unto the LORD; revealed things belong to us and our children
Both secret and revealed things belong to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Secret things belong unto the LORD; revealed things belong to us and our children
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:29 distinguishes between God's hidden knowledge and the revealed instructions that are given to the people to obey.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 29:23 where the land is compared to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim?
options: Metaphor
Chiasm
Simile
Anthropomorphism
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:23 uses a simile by likening the desolation of the land to the destruction of well-known cities, emphasizing the severity of judgment.

questions.question: The word 'covenant' in Hebrew is 'berith'. What is the primary significance of this term as used in Deuteronomy 29:1?
options: A casual agreement between friends
A binding legal and relational agreement between God and Israel
A secret pact among kings
A ceremonial feast
questions.correctAnswer: A binding legal and relational agreement between God and Israel
questions.explanation: In Deuteronomy 29:1, 'covenant' (berith) denotes a solemn, binding agreement establishing a relationship between God and Israel, foundational to their identity and obligations.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God's judgment on apostasy described in Deuteronomy 29:27-28?
options: Jeremiah 30:7
Ezekiel 20:33-38
Psalm 23
Proverbs 3:5-6
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 20:33-38
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:33-38 parallels Deuteronomy 29:27-28 by describing God's purification of Israel through judgment for their disobedience and idolatry.

questions.question: How does the theme of covenant in Deuteronomy 29 relate to the New Testament concept of the 'new covenant'?
options: The old covenant was completely replaced without connection
The new covenant fulfills and renews the covenantal relationship introduced in Deuteronomy 29
The new covenant rejects all laws given in Deuteronomy
There is no relation between the two covenants
questions.correctAnswer: The new covenant fulfills and renews the covenantal relationship introduced in Deuteronomy 29
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29's covenant concepts are foundational, and the New Testament (e.g., Jeremiah 31:31-34, Luke 22:20) presents the new covenant as a fulfillment and renewal of God's promises.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 29:20 indicates that the LORD will spare the man who blesses himself in his heart despite hearing the curses.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:20 explicitly states the LORD will not spare that man; instead, His anger and jealousy will be against him, leading to curses and blotted-out name.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 29:5 highlights that during the 40 years in the wilderness, the Israelites' clothes and shoes did not wear out, symbolizing God's provision.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:5 notes that despite 40 years in the desert, their garments and shoes remained intact, demonstrating God's sustaining care.

questions.question: Which phrase in Deuteronomy 29:19 metaphorically describes a root that produces bitterness and distress among the people?
options: Root that beareth gall and wormwood
Fruit that bringeth sweetness and joy
Seed of righteousness
Branch of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Root that beareth gall and wormwood
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:19 uses this metaphor to describe those whose hearts turn away from God, causing bitterness and trouble within the community.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:16-17 highlight the historical and cultural context of Israel's journey and encounter with surrounding nations?
options: By ignoring other nations' customs
By recounting Israel's passage through nations and exposure to their idolatry
By focusing solely on Egyptian culture
By praising the nations' gods
questions.correctAnswer: By recounting Israel's passage through nations and exposure to their idolatry
questions.explanation: These verses recall Israel's history traveling through nations with abominations and idols, underscoring the constant temptation to idolatry in their cultural context.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 29 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 29 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 29:6 indicate about the purpose of Israel's forty years in the wilderness?
options: To make them strong warriors
To know that the LORD is their God
To teach them agriculture
To prepare them to conquer Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: To know that the LORD is their God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:6 states that Israel neither ate bread nor drank wine or strong drink during this time 'that ye might know that I am the LORD your God,' emphasizing the purpose was to reveal God's identity and sovereignty.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Deuteronomy 29:20 regarding the punishment of those who turn away from God?
options: God's mercy
God's jealousy and anger
God's patience
God's forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: God's jealousy and anger
questions.explanation: Verse 29:20 mentions 'the anger of the LORD and his jealousy shall smoke against that man,' emphasizing God's attribute of holy jealousy and righteous anger against sin.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:29, how are 'secret things' and 'revealed things' distinguished in relation to God and His people?
options: Secret things belong to humans; revealed things belong to God
Secret things belong to angels; revealed things belong to prophets
Secret things belong to God; revealed things belong to us and our children
Secret things belong to kings; revealed things belong to priests
questions.correctAnswer: Secret things belong to God; revealed things belong to us and our children
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:29 explicitly states that 'The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children,' teaching divine sovereignty in hidden matters and human responsibility in revealed truth.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Deuteronomy 29:5 and 29:6 convey about God's providence and care for Israel?
options: God provided material blessings but not spiritual guidance
God preserved Israel physically and taught them to know Him
God left Israel to fend for themselves in the wilderness
God punished Israel for their disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God preserved Israel physically and taught them to know Him
questions.explanation: Verse 29:5 notes God preserved their clothing and shoes for 40 years, and 29:6 indicates their lack of food and drink was purposeful so they might know God. Together these show God's providential care and the goal of relational knowledge.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:18 describe the spiritual danger of turning away from God in covenant context?
options: A person becomes a source of bitterness and corruption
A person gains more knowledge of other gods
A person is immediately forgiven
A person is blessed with prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: A person becomes a source of bitterness and corruption
questions.explanation: Verse 29:18 warns against hearts turning away to serve other gods, likening such a person to 'a root that beareth gall and wormwood,' symbolizing bitterness and destructive influence.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 29:13 reveal about the covenant’s purpose for Israel’s identity?
options: To establish Israel as a kingdom over other nations
To make Israel a people belonging to God and God to be their God
To allow Israel to conquer all other peoples
To separate Israel from all other tribes forever
questions.correctAnswer: To make Israel a people belonging to God and God to be their God
questions.explanation: Verse 29:13 states the covenant aims 'that he may establish thee...for a people unto himself, and that he may be unto thee a God,' highlighting the covenantal relationship central to Israel’s identity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illuminated by Deuteronomy 29:9's exhortation to 'keep therefore the words of this covenant, and do them'?
options: Doctrine of justification by faith alone
Doctrine of sanctification and covenant obedience
Doctrine of predestination
Doctrine of universal salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of sanctification and covenant obedience
questions.explanation: The verse commands active obedience to covenant words for prosperity, reflecting the doctrine that sanctification involves living in faithful covenant obedience.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 29:7-8, what historical event serves as a foundation for Israel's possession of the land?
options: The fall of Jericho
Battles against Sihon and Og, kings of Heshbon and Bashan
The crossing of the Red Sea
The giving of the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: Battles against Sihon and Og, kings of Heshbon and Bashan
questions.explanation: Verses 29:7-8 recount how Israel defeated these kings and took their land, giving it as inheritance to tribes, establishing a historical basis for possession.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:14-15 expand the scope of the covenant beyond the present generation?
options: It applies only to the elders present
It includes those present and those not present on that day
It excludes foreigners living among Israel
It applies only to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: It includes those present and those not present on that day
questions.explanation: Verses 29:14-15 state the covenant is not just with those present but also with those absent, indicating covenant continuity across generations.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 29:21 teach about the consequences of covenant disobedience for an individual within Israel?
options: The individual is blessed and prospered
The individual is separated unto evil and cursed
The individual is immediately forgiven
The individual is removed from the land by human judges
questions.correctAnswer: The individual is separated unto evil and cursed
questions.explanation: Verse 29:21 declares the LORD will separate the disobedient 'unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel,' reflecting divine judgment for covenant breach.

questions.question: What is the apologetic implication of Deuteronomy 29:25-28 against the sceptic’s claim that God’s judgment is arbitrary?
options: God’s judgment is random and without cause
God’s judgment is a response to covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry
God’s judgment is based on human politics
God’s judgment is only symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is a response to covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry
questions.explanation: These verses show God’s anger and judgment come because Israel forsook the covenant and served false gods, demonstrating that divine punishment is just and purposeful, countering claims of arbitrariness.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:10-12 emphasize the inclusivity of the covenant community?
options: Only men of fighting age are included
Everyone including captains, elders, officers, women, children, and even strangers are included
Only priests and Levites are included
Only Israelites born in the land are included
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone including captains, elders, officers, women, children, and even strangers are included
questions.explanation: Verses 29:10-12 list a broad range of people present to enter the covenant, showing God’s covenant includes all members of the community and resident foreigners.

questions.question: What does the imagery in Deuteronomy 29:23 comparing the land to 'brimstone, and salt, and burning' teach about divine judgment?
options: That judgment leaves the land fruitful and blessed
That judgment results in desolation like Sodom and Gomorrah
That judgment is temporary and quickly reversed
That judgment is symbolic with no real effect
questions.correctAnswer: That judgment results in desolation like Sodom and Gomorrah
questions.explanation: Verse 29:23 likens the land’s devastation to the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, illustrating that God's judgment produces total desolation as a consequence of sin.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine revelation and human responsibility is conveyed by Deuteronomy 29:4 and 29:29?
options: God does not reveal anything to humans
God has given humans heart, eyes, and ears to perceive revealed things, but secret things remain with God
Humans can fully understand all divine secrets
Humans are responsible for secret things
questions.correctAnswer: God has given humans heart, eyes, and ears to perceive revealed things, but secret things remain with God
questions.explanation: Verse 29:4 laments Israel’s lack of perception despite signs, while 29:29 distinguishes secret things belonging to God and revealed things belonging to people, together teaching that God reveals what humans must know, leaving some mysteries to divine sovereignty.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 29:16-17 provide a theological warning against idolatry based on Israel’s past experiences?
options: It encourages Israel to adopt foreign idols
It reminds Israel of the abominations and idols of the nations they passed through to avoid similar sin
It ignores Israel’s past and focuses only on the future
It suggests idols are harmless
questions.correctAnswer: It reminds Israel of the abominations and idols of the nations they passed through to avoid similar sin
questions.explanation: These verses recall the idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold among other nations, serving as a warning to Israel not to imitate their abominations.
